claim: There is no apparent opening or closing motion between the domains in the Dm1 to Dm2 transition.
source: On a global scale (Figure 2), the Dm2 state is 'twisted' relative to the Dm1 state: with the two models aligned on subunit ND1 in the 'heel' of the complex, the hydrophilic and membrane domains twist in opposite directions (there is no apparent opening or closing motion between the domains).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison.

claim: A similar twisting relationship was identified between the active and deactive resting states of mammalian complex I.
source: A similar twisting relationship was identified between the active and deactive resting states of mammalian complex I (Zhu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Standard biochemical assays used to detect the presence of the mammalian deactive state did not detect any deactive Drosophila enzyme, even after incubation at 37°C to promote deactivation.
source: However, standard biochemical assays used to detect the presence of the mammalian deactive state did not detect any deactive Drosophila enzyme, even after incubation at 37°C to promote deactivation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating that Dm2 is not directly comparable to the mammalian-type deactive state.
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dm2 is not directly comparable to the mammalian-type deactive state.
source: However, standard biochemical assays used to detect the presence of the mammalian deactive state did not detect any deactive Drosophila enzyme, even after incubation at 37°C to promote deactivation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), indicating that Dm2 is not directly comparable to the mammalian-type deactive state.
evidence: This is an inference based on biochemical assay results.

claim: In the mammalian deactive state, the equivalent residue to ND3-Cys41 is exposed to solution and can be derivatised by N-ethylmaleimide (NEM).
source: In the mammalian deactive state, the equivalent residue to ND3-Cys41 (we use Drosophila numbering throughout) is exposed to solution and can be derivatised by N-ethylmaleimide (NEM), preventing reactivation of the deactive enzyme and its return to catalysis, whereas in the active state ND3-Cys41 is buried (Galkin et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Derivatisation of ND3-Cys41 by NEM prevents reactivation of the deactive enzyme and its return to catalysis.
source: In the mammalian deactive state, the equivalent residue to ND3-Cys41 (we use Drosophila numbering throughout) is exposed to solution and can be derivatised by N-ethylmaleimide (NEM), preventing reactivation of the deactive enzyme and its return to catalysis, whereas in the active state ND3-Cys41 is buried (Galkin et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: In the mammalian active state, ND3-Cys41 is buried.
source: In the mammalian deactive state, the equivalent residue to ND3-Cys41 (we use Drosophila numbering throughout) is exposed to solution and can be derivatised by N-ethylmaleimide (NEM), preventing reactivation of the deactive enzyme and its return to catalysis, whereas in the active state ND3-Cys41 is buried (Galkin et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Either ND3-Cys41 is buried and inaccessible to derivatisation in all three Dm1, Dm2, and Dm3 states, or ND3-Cys41 is exposed in one or more state that is completely inactive.
source: Our assays suggest that either ND3-Cys41 is buried and inaccessible to derivatisation in all three Dm1, Dm2, and Dm3 states, or that ND3-Cys41 is exposed in one or more state that is completely inactive, being unable to either reactivate or catalyse.
evidence: This is an inference based on biochemical assay results.

claim: The most obvious global feature of the Dm3 state is that the membrane domain appears 'cracked' at the interface between ND2 and ND4.
source: For the Dm3 state, the most obvious global feature (Figure 2) is that the membrane domain appears 'cracked' at the interface between ND2 and ND4; the density for the adjacent subunit NDUFA11 is disordered, along with the adjacent N-terminus of NDUFS2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: In the Dm3 state, the density for the adjacent subunit NDUFA11 is disordered, along with the adjacent N-terminus of NDUFS2.
source: For the Dm3 state, the most obvious global feature (Figure 2) is that the membrane domain appears 'cracked' at the interface between ND2 and ND4; the density for the adjacent subunit NDUFA11 is disordered, along with the adjacent N-terminus of NDUFS2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The characteristics of the Dm3 state resemble those of the 'slack' state of bovine complex I.
source: These characteristics resemble those of the 'slack' state of bovine complex I (Chung et al., 2022b; Zhu et al., 2016), which is of uncertain biochemical and physiological relevance and which may result from destabilisation of the membrane-intrinsic domain following extraction from the membrane and delipidation by detergents during purification.
evidence: This is a comparison based on structural similarity, supported by citations.

claim: The 'slack' state of bovine complex I is of uncertain biochemical and physiological relevance.
source: These characteristics resemble those of the 'slack' state of bovine complex I (Chung et al., 2022b; Zhu et al., 2016), which is of uncertain biochemical and physiological relevance and which may result from destabilisation of the membrane-intrinsic domain following extraction from the membrane and delipidation by detergents during purification.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current understanding, supported by citations.

claim: The 'slack' state may result from destabilisation of the membrane-intrinsic domain following extraction from the membrane and delipidation by detergents during purification.
source: These characteristics resemble those of the 'slack' state of bovine complex I (Chung et al., 2022b; Zhu et al., 2016), which is of uncertain biochemical and physiological relevance and which may result from destabilisation of the membrane-intrinsic domain following extraction from the membrane and delipidation by detergents during purification.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations.

claim: In the Dm1 state of Drosophila complex I, all local features are unambiguously in the active state.
source: In the Dm1 state of Drosophila complex I, these features are all unambiguously in the active state (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 3a.

claim: In the Dm1 state, ND6-TMH3 is clearly α-helical and does not contain the π-bulge that is characteristic of the deactive state.
source: First, ND6-TMH3 is clearly α-helical, it does not contain the π-bulge that is characteristic of the deactive state, and ND1-TMH4 is clearly in the 'bent' conformation of the active state (with Tyr149 pointing toward the E-channel), not the straight conformation of the deactive state (with Tyr149 pointing away from the E-channel).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis.

claim: In the Dm1 state, ND1-TMH4 is clearly in the 'bent' conformation of the active state (with Tyr149 pointing toward the E-channel), not the straight conformation of the deactive state (with Tyr149 pointing away from the E-channel).
source: First, ND6-TMH3 is clearly α-helical, it does not contain the π-bulge that is characteristic of the deactive state, and ND1-TMH4 is clearly in the 'bent' conformation of the active state (with Tyr149 pointing toward the E-channel), not the straight conformation of the deactive state (with Tyr149 pointing away from the E-channel).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis.

claim: In the Dm1 state, the densities for the NDUFS2-β1−β2 loop, the ND3-TMH1−2 loop, and the ND1-TMH5−6 loop are all well-defined and their conformations match the mammalian active-state conformations.
source: Second, the densities for the NDUFS2-β1−β2 loop that carries the His97 ligand to bound ubiquinone, the ND3-TMH1−2 loop that carries Cys41 (the biochemical marker of the mammalian active/deactive states), and the ND1-TMH5−6 loop, are all well-defined in the Dm1 density map and their conformations match the mammalian active-state conformations (they are not disordered as in the deactive state).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis.

claim: In the Dm1 state, ND3-Cys41, NDUFS2-His93, and ND1-Tyr134 meet in a trigonal junction at the top of ND1-TMH4.
source: ND3-Cys41, NDUFS2-His93, and ND1-Tyr134 meet in a trigonal junction at the top of ND1-TMH4 (Grba and Hirst, 2020), as they do in the active state (Figure 3c).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 3c and citation.

claim: In the Dm1 state, the FRASPR motif in NDUFS7 that includes Arg119 matches its conformation in the mammalian active, not deactive, state.
source: Finally, the FRASPR motif in NDUFS7 that includes Arg119 matches its conformation in the mammalian active, not deactive, state.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison.

claim: The ubiquinone-binding site in the Dm1 state is sealed and closed from the matrix.
source: Importantly, as expected from the ordered states of the loop structures that form the ubiquinone-binding site, the site is sealed and closed from the matrix (Figure 3b and c) as in the mammalian active state, not open to the matrix as in the deactive state (Agip et al., 2018; Blaza et al., 2018; Chung et al., 2022a; Chung et al., 2022b; Zhu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 3b and c, and citations.

claim: The Dm1 state is a catalytically competent state, ready to bind and reduce the extended and hydrophobic ubiquinone-9 or ubiquinone-10 substrate.
source: This observation indicates that the Dm1 state is a catalytically competent state, ready to bind and reduce the extended and hydrophobic ubiquinone-9 or ubiquinone-10 substrate (referred to as Q9 for brevity).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observation of the sealed ubiquinone-binding site.

claim: Density for Q9 is observed within the ubiquinone-binding site in the Dm1 state.
source: Indeed, density for Q9 is observed within the site, although the Q9 is only partially inserted, with its ubiquinone-headgroup in the central section of the channel, rather than ligated to the two proton-donor ligands NDUFS2-His97 and NDUFS2-Tyr146 as required for its reduction (Baradaran et al., 2013; Tocilescu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis.

claim: The Q9 in the Dm1 state is only partially inserted, with its ubiquinone-headgroup in the central section of the channel.
source: Indeed, density for Q9 is observed within the site, although the Q9 is only partially inserted, with its ubiquinone-headgroup in the central section of the channel, rather than ligated to the two proton-donor ligands NDUFS2-His97 and NDUFS2-Tyr146 as required for its reduction (Baradaran et al., 2013; Tocilescu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis.

claim: The Q9 headgroup in the Dm1 state is not ligated to the two proton-donor ligands NDUFS2-His97 and NDUFS2-Tyr146 as required for its reduction.
source: Indeed, density for Q9 is observed within the site, although the Q9 is only partially inserted, with its ubiquinone-headgroup in the central section of the channel, rather than ligated to the two proton-donor ligands NDUFS2-His97 and NDUFS2-Tyr146 as required for its reduction (Baradaran et al., 2013; Tocilescu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis and citations.

claim: Partially inserted ubiquinones have been observed previously in several different species and states of complex I.
source: Partially inserted ubiquinones have been observed previously in several different species and states of complex I (Gu et al., 2022; Kampjut and Sazanov, 2020; Kravchuk et al., 2022; Parey et al., 2019; Soufari et al., 2020), but the headgroup typically sits slightly lower down the channel than observed here, in an array of positions distributed largely around the hydrophilic 'kink' of the channel (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Drosophila Q9 headgroup is bound 11 and 14 Å away, respectively, from its proposed ligating partners NDUFS2-His97 and NDUFS2-Tyr146.
source: The Drosophila Q9 headgroup is bound 11 and 14 Å away, respectively, from its proposed ligating partners NDUFS2-His97 and NDUFS2-Tyr146, between the '1F' site described in Sus scrofa complex I (Gu et al., 2022) and the 'Qm' site described in Escherichia coli (Kravchuk et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from structural analysis, with citations for comparison.

claim: The wide spectrum of headgroup positions identified in different complex I structures suggests that substrates may shuttle in a step-wise manner, occupying numerous sites of localised energy minima.
source: The wide spectrum of headgroup positions identified in different complex I structures suggests that substrates may shuttle in a step-wise manner, occupying numerous sites of localised energy minima (Chung et al., 2021; Hoias Teixeira and Menegon Arantes, 2019; Warnau et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on structural observations, supported by citations.

claim: In the mammalian complex, two subunits, NDUFA5 on the hydrophilic domain and NDUFA10 on the membrane domain, meet in the corner of the L-shape forming an interface between the two domains.
source: In the mammalian complex, two subunits, NDUFA5 on the hydrophilic domain and NDUFA10 on the membrane domain, meet in the corner of the L-shape forming an interface between the two domains.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammalian complex I structure.

claim: Upon deactivation of the mammalian enzyme, the altered disposition of the hydrophilic and membrane domains changes the NDUFA5/NDUFA10 interface and decreases their contact area.
source: Upon deactivation of the mammalian enzyme, the altered disposition of the hydrophilic and membrane domains changes the NDUFA5/NDUFA10 interface and decreases their contact area (Agip et al., 2018; Zhu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Subunit NDUFA5 lies in an intermediate position in the Dm1 state compared to the mammalian active and deactive states.
source: Both subunits are present in the Drosophila enzyme, and Figure 4a compares their relative positions in the Dm1 active state to their relative positions in the active and deactive mammalian states. With the structures aligned to subunit NDUFA10, subunit NDUFA5, which is dominated by a three-helix bundle, clearly lies in an intermediate position in the Dm1 state, it does not overlay its position in the mammalian active state.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The N-terminus of hydrophilic-domain subunit NDUFS2 that runs along the top of the membrane domain is in an intermediate position in the Dm1 state.
source: The N-terminus of hydrophilic-domain subunit NDUFS2 that runs along the top of the membrane domain is also in an intermediate position.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison.

claim: The NDUFA5/NDUFA10 contact area in the Dm1 state matches closely to that observed in the mammalian active state (388 Å2 vs. 354 Å2).
source: However, the NDUFA5/NDUFA10 contact area still matches closely to that observed in the mammalian active state (388 Å2 vs. 354 and 131 Å2 in the bovine active and deactive states [Chung et al., 2022b], respectively), and the NDUFA5/NDUFA10 interface is clearly different as it incorporates the N-terminus of the NDUFS4 subunit (residues 33–49; Figure 4b), which is substantially extended relative to in mammalian species (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from structural analysis, with citation for comparison.

claim: The NDUFA5/NDUFA10 interface in the Dm1 state incorporates the N-terminus of the NDUFS4 subunit (residues 33–49), which is substantially extended relative to in mammalian species.
source: However, the NDUFA5/NDUFA10 contact area still matches closely to that observed in the mammalian active state (388 Å2 vs. 354 and 131 Å2 in the bovine active and deactive states [Chung et al., 2022b], respectively), and the NDUFA5/NDUFA10 interface is clearly different as it incorporates the N-terminus of the NDUFS4 subunit (residues 33–49; Figure 4b), which is substantially extended relative to in mammalian species (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 4b and 4c.

claim: Contacts between the NDUFS4 N-terminal 'tether' and subunits NDUFA5 and NDUFA10 of 182 and 427 Å2, respectively, further stabilise the interface in the Dm1 state.
source: Contacts between the NDUFS4 N-terminal 'tether' and subunits NDUFA5 and NDUFA10 of 182 and 427 Å2, respectively, further stabilise the interface and, by extension, the relative disposition of the hydrophilic and membrane domains in the Drosophila Dm1 active state.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from structural analysis.

claim: The NDUFS4 N-terminal 'tether' stabilises the relative disposition of the hydrophilic and membrane domains in the Drosophila Dm1 active state.
source: Contacts between the NDUFS4 N-terminal 'tether' and subunits NDUFA5 and NDUFA10 of 182 and 427 Å2, respectively, further stabilise the interface and, by extension, the relative disposition of the hydrophilic and membrane domains in the Drosophila Dm1 active state.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis.

claim: Subunits NDUFS2, NDUFS7, and ND1 that constitute the ubiquinone-binding site overlay closely between the mammalian and Drosophila active-state structures (RMSD 0.574).
source: Further comparison of the mammalian and Drosophila active-state structures showed that subunits NDUFS2, NDUFS7, and ND1 that constitute the ubiquinone-binding site (Figure 3), overlay closely (RMSD 0.574 between Dm1 and the bovine active state [PDB ID: 7QSK]; Chung et al., 2022b) but that the structures then diverge along the membrane domain, shifting the position and orientation of subunit ND2 (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from structural comparison, with citation.

claim: The structures of mammalian and Drosophila complex I diverge along the membrane domain, shifting the position and orientation of subunit ND2.
source: Further comparison of the mammalian and Drosophila active-state structures showed that subunits NDUFS2, NDUFS7, and ND1 that constitute the ubiquinone-binding site (Figure 3), overlay closely (RMSD 0.574 between Dm1 and the bovine active state [PDB ID: 7QSK]; Chung et al., 2022b) but that the structures then diverge along the membrane domain, shifting the position and orientation of subunit ND2 (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The arrangement of the TMHs in subunit ND6 clearly differs between the Drosophila and mammalian enzymes.
source: Within the connecting subdomain between ND1 and ND2 that contains subunits ND3, ND6, and ND4L, the arrangement of the TMHs in subunit ND6 (Figure 5b) clearly differs between the Drosophila and mammalian enzymes (despite them both containing a fully α-helical ND6-TMH3).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 5b.

claim: ND6-TMH4 is markedly displaced in Drosophila complex I, enhancing a cleft between ND6 and ND1 in which three phospholipid molecules are observed.
source: In particular, ND6-TMH4 is markedly displaced, enhancing a cleft between ND6 and ND1 in which three phospholipid molecules are observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The position of ND6-TMH4 is remarkably variable between different species and states of complex I.
source: The position of ND6-TMH4 is remarkably variable between different species and states of complex I, suggesting that it is not functionally important (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The variability of ND6-TMH4 position suggests that it is not functionally important.
source: The position of ND6-TMH4 is remarkably variable between different species and states of complex I, suggesting that it is not functionally important (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations.

claim: Structures around ND6-TMH4 vary between Drosophila and mammalian complex I.
source: Structures around ND6-TMH4 also vary (Figure 5b and c): (i) the ND6-TMH4–5 loop is restructured and its β-hairpin disrupted by neighbouring ND4L-TMH1, (ii) ND6-TMH1 is displaced away from TMH4 to avoid steric clashes, (iii) the ND6-TMH3–4 loop is restructured to accommodate the movement of TMH4, and (iv) the C-terminal loop of NDUFA9, located just above the reordered ND6-TMH3–4 loop, is retracted.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison shown in Figure 5b and c.

claim: The ND3-TMH1–2 loop remains ordered with ND3-Cys41 occluded in the Drosophila Dm1 state.
source: The ND3-TMH1–2 loop, which is also adjacent to the restructured region, remains ordered with ND3-Cys41 occluded (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The residues of the central axis that link the terminus of the E-channel to the start of the first antiporter-like subunit (ND2) are not affected by the altered connecting subdomain structure.
source: Strikingly, the residues of the central axis that link the terminus of the E-channel to the start of the first antiporter-like subunit (ND2) are not affected by the altered connecting subdomain structure, which thus adjusts the relative disposition of subunits in the hydrophilic and membrane domains in the Drosophila Dm1 state without affecting the catalytic machinery of the active state structure.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis.

claim: The altered connecting subdomain structure adjusts the relative disposition of subunits in the hydrophilic and membrane domains in the Drosophila Dm1 state without affecting the catalytic machinery of the active state structure.
source: Strikingly, the residues of the central axis that link the terminus of the E-channel to the start of the first antiporter-like subunit (ND2) are not affected by the altered connecting subdomain structure, which thus adjusts the relative disposition of subunits in the hydrophilic and membrane domains in the Drosophila Dm1 state without affecting the catalytic machinery of the active state structure.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis.

claim: Inspection of the set of local features in the core subunits revealed that both the Dm2 and Dm3 states also most closely correspond to the mammalian active state.
source: Inspection of the set of local features in the core subunits (Agip et al., 2018; Blaza et al., 2018; Chung et al., 2022a; Chung et al., 2022b; Letts et al., 2019; Zhu et al., 2016) that differentiate the mammalian active and deactive states in the two minor states revealed that both the Dm2 and Dm3 states also most closely correspond to the mammalian active state.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis and citations.

claim: In the Dm2 state, two features of the mammalian deactive state are present: a π-bulge has formed in ND6-TMH3 and ND1-TMH4-Tyr149 has 'flipped' its conformation.
source: Figure 6a shows that, in the Dm2 state, two features of the mammalian deactive state are present: a π-bulge has formed in ND6-TMH3 and ND1-TMH4-Tyr149 has 'flipped' its conformation (Chung et al., 2022b; Grba and Hirst, 2020; Kampjut and Sazanov, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 6a and citations.

claim: In the Dm2 state, all the other key elements remain in their active states, including ND1-TMH4, which remains in its bent conformation.
source: However, all the other key elements remain in their active states, including ND1-TMH4, which remains in its bent conformation, and as a result the ubiquinone-binding site remains enclosed and sealed from the matrix (Figure 6b and c).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 6b and c.

claim: In the Dm2 state, the ubiquinone-binding site remains enclosed and sealed from the matrix.
source: However, all the other key elements remain in their active states, including ND1-TMH4, which remains in its bent conformation, and as a result the ubiquinone-binding site remains enclosed and sealed from the matrix (Figure 6b and c).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 6b and c.

claim: The same is true for the Dm3 state (ubiquinone-binding site remains enclosed and sealed).
source: The same is true for the Dm3 state (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The trigonal junction between ND3-Cys41, NDUFS2-His93, and ND1-Tyr134 is preserved in all three states (Dm1, Dm2, Dm3).
source: Notably, the trigonal junction between ND3-Cys41, NDUFS2-His93, and ND1-Tyr134 (Grba and Hirst, 2020) is preserved in all three states, occluding the Cys from the matrix and explaining why a mammalian-type deactive state of Drosophila complex I could not be trapped in biochemical assays (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis and biochemical assay data, with citation.

claim: The preservation of the trigonal junction occludes ND3-Cys41 from the matrix and explains why a mammalian-type deactive state of Drosophila complex I could not be trapped in biochemical assays.
source: Notably, the trigonal junction between ND3-Cys41, NDUFS2-His93, and ND1-Tyr134 (Grba and Hirst, 2020) is preserved in all three states, occluding the Cys from the matrix and explaining why a mammalian-type deactive state of Drosophila complex I could not be trapped in biochemical assays (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural and biochemical data.

claim: Drosophila complex I does not form an 'open' resting state, it rests only in 'closed' conformations with the ubiquinone-binding site enclosed and sealed from the matrix.
source: We conclude that, in contrast to the mammalian enzyme, Drosophila complex I does not form an 'open' resting state, it rests only in 'closed' conformations with the ubiquinone-binding site enclosed and sealed from the matrix.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on structural analysis of all three states.

claim: The structures determined here for Drosophila complex I confirm its close relationships with mammalian complex I.
source: The structures determined here for Drosophila complex I confirm its close relationships with mammalian complex I and thus its potential as a powerful genetically tractable model system for studying mammalian-specific aspects of complex I biology.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural data presented.

claim: Drosophila complex I has potential as a powerful genetically tractable model system for studying mammalian-specific aspects of complex I biology.
source: The structures determined here for Drosophila complex I confirm its close relationships with mammalian complex I and thus its potential as a powerful genetically tractable model system for studying mammalian-specific aspects of complex I biology.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural similarity and known characteristics of Drosophila.

claim: The close-to-identical subunit compositions and structures of the mammalian and Drosophila enzymes enable genetic approaches to be applied to elucidate the roles of the supernumerary subunits, the assembly pathway, and the detrimental effects of clinically identified pathological point mutations.
source: The close-to-identical subunit compositions and structures of the mammalian and Drosophila enzymes now enable genetic approaches to be applied to elucidate, for example, the roles of the supernumerary subunits, the assembly pathway, and the detrimental effects of clinically identified pathological point mutations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural similarity.

claim: These aspects can be studied in physiologically relevant in vivo environments and in specific cell types and tissues in Drosophila.
source: Importantly, these aspects can be studied in physiologically relevant in vivo environments and in specific cell types and tissues, extending the scope of earlier studies in cultured mammalian cells (Guerrero-Castillo et al., 2017; Stroud et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on the capabilities of Drosophila as a model organism, with citations.

claim: The Drosophila enzyme, despite its remarkable similarity to the mammalian enzyme, does not undergo the full mammalian-type active/deactive transition.
source: However, our structures also reveal limitations in Drosophila as a model organism for complex I, as the Drosophila enzyme, despite its remarkable similarity to the mammalian enzyme, does not undergo the full mammalian-type active/deactive transition.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on structural and biochemical data.

claim: The cryo-EM analyses revealed the major class of enzyme particle (Dm1) in the active resting state, with all the characteristics of the mammalian active state enzyme.
source: Our cryo-EM analyses revealed the major class of enzyme particle (Dm1) in the active resting state, with all the characteristics of the mammalian active state enzyme.
evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM data.

claim: Two minor states (Dm2 and Dm3) also more closely resemble the active state.
source: Two minor states (Dm2 and Dm3) also more closely resemble the active state, and we were unable to either detect a mammalian-type deactive resting state in biochemical assays, or to generate one by incubation of the enzyme at 37°C (the method used to deactivate mammalian complex I).
evidence: This is supported by structural and biochemical data.

claim: The authors were unable to either detect a mammalian-type deactive resting state in biochemical assays, or to generate one by incubation of the enzyme at 37°C.
source: Two minor states (Dm2 and Dm3) also more closely resemble the active state, and we were unable to either detect a mammalian-type deactive resting state in biochemical assays, or to generate one by incubation of the enzyme at 37°C (the method used to deactivate mammalian complex I).
evidence: This is supported by biochemical assay data.

claim: The functional consequences of conversion to the Dm2 state are currently unknown, most notably whether it is able to catalyse RET.
source: However, we note that our biochemical assay relies on the availability of ND3-Cys41, just one characteristic that distinguishes the mammalian active and deactive states; the functional consequences of conversion to the Dm2 state are currently unknown, most notably whether it is (like the mammalian active state) able to catalyse RET, or (like the mammalian deactive state) unable to do so.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of the limitations of the current study.

claim: Comparison of the Dm1 (active) and Dm2 (twisted) structures suggests that the Dm2 state is a relaxed state, which may be considered a structurally curtailed form of the full mammalian-type deactive transition.
source: Comparison of the Dm1 (active) and Dm2 (twisted) structures of Drosophila complex I determined here suggests that the Dm2 state is a relaxed state, which may be considered a structurally curtailed form of the full mammalian-type deactive transition (Agip et al., 2018; Blaza et al., 2018; Chung et al., 2022a; Chung et al., 2022b; Zhu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on structural comparison, with citations.

claim: In changes that also occur in the mammalian transition, a π-bulge forms in ND6-TMH3, and the nearby sidechain of ND1-TMH4-Tyr149 flips in conformation.
source: In changes that also occur in the mammalian transition, a π-bulge forms in ND6-TMH3, and the nearby sidechain of ND1-TMH4-Tyr149 flips in conformation.
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison.

claim: These changes are expected to alter the connectivity between the E-channel and the central axis of charged residues along the membrane domain.
source: Although water molecules cannot be resolved in our structures, these changes are expected to alter the connectivity between the E-channel and the central axis of charged residues along the membrane domain as reported previously for mammalian, yeast, and bacterial species (Agip et al., 2018; Blaza et al., 2018; Chung et al., 2022b; Grba and Hirst, 2020; Kampjut and Sazanov, 2020; Kravchuk et al., 2022; Parey et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations and prior knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: The limited and local changes observed in the ND6 region result in a limited twisting of the global conformation in the Dm2 state.

source: However, the cascade of changes that also occurs in the mammalian-type deactive transition does not follow: ND1-TMH4 does not straighten its conformation, the trigonal junction between ND3-Cys41, NDUFS2-His93, and ND1-Tyr134 is preserved, and so the conformational change from ND6-TMH3 does not propagate to the ubiquinone-binding site, which remains fully ordered, sealed from the matrix, and in its active state (Figure 6).

claim: This lack of direct correlation between the status of the α-helix/π-bulge and the structuring of the ubiquinone-binding site argues against a concerted and structurally enforced connection between them being crucial for catalysis.

claim: The Drosophila Dm2 structure is the first example in which the π-bulge and a fully ordered, active ubiquinone-binding site have been observed together.
source: Although structures of complex I from other (non-mammalian) species have also been reported with a π-bulge in ND6-TMH3 but without the 'opening' of the ubiquinone-binding site observed in the mammalian deactive state (Chung et al., 2022a), our Drosophila Dm2 structure is the first example in which the π-bulge and a fully ordered, active ubiquinone-binding site have been observed together.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding, supported by citation.

source: Alternatively, it is possible that enzyme twisting, induced by loss of the NDUFS4 tether from the NDUFA5/NDUFA10 interface during purification, causes the π-bulge to form: this possibility may be addressed in future by genetic truncation of the NDUFS4 tether from the N-terminus of the mature subunit.
